note: ㅂ-irregular: 흥미로워요.

ex.en: That documentary was really interesting.
The class is more interesting than I expected.
That's an interesting story. Tell me more.

note: Causative of 먹다.

ex.en: Did you feed the baby?
I'll feed the dog and then head out.
I gave my kid cold medicine.

note: Verb: 정리하다.

ex.s: 주말에 방 정리 좀 해야 돼요.
ex.en: I need to tidy my room this weekend.
I'll organize the meeting notes and send them to you.
Have you finished sorting out your luggage?

note: Staff address customers directly as 손님.

ex.en: We have guests coming this evening.
Are you ready to order?
This shop always has lots of customers.
I'm so worn out from all the work today.
I got exhausted playing with the kids.
I get tired quickly in hot weather.

note: 검색하다: to search, look up online.

ex.en: I looked it up online.
I'm searching for good restaurants nearby.
There are too many search results.
The payment has gone through.
Turn it back on once the update is complete.
The hotel booking is done.
I left my phone in the classroom.
What floor is my kid's classroom on?
I started going to a yoga class.

note: e.g., 위암 stomach cancer, 폐암 lung cancer.

ex.en: My grandfather had cancer surgery.

ex.s: 담배는 암의 원인이 될 수 있어요.
ex.en: Smoking can cause cancer.
My friend's mom beat cancer.

note: 목숨(을) 걸고: as if one's life depended on it.

ex.s: 그 의사가 우리 아빠 목숨을 구했어요.
ex.en: That doctor saved my dad's life.
Seat belts save lives.
I studied like my life depended on it for the exam.
My child starts kindergarten next year.
The kindergarten teacher called.
I'll pick the kid up when kindergarten lets out.

en: to approach, come up to; draw near

ex.en: The dog came up wagging its tail.
The exam is coming up, so I'm worried.
A stranger came up asking for directions.
There was a huge crowd at the concert.

ex.s: 그 영화 관객이 천만 명 넘었대요.
ex.en: They say that movie topped ten million viewers.
The whole audience stood up and clapped.

note: More formal than 기차; used in announcements and on tickets.

ex.en: What time does the next train come?
The train left ten minutes late.
I booked a train to Busan.

note: Everyday word is 빨갛다; 붉다 for faces, sunsets, leaves.

ex.en: The evening sky turned red.
My face turned red from embarrassment.
It's autumn, so the leaves are red.
Please add extra cheese to the pizza.
Is there any cheese left in the fridge?
Say 'cheese' for the photo!

note: Different word from the verb 세다 'to count'.

ex.en: The wind is really strong today.
This liquor is stronger than I thought.
My younger sibling is really stubborn.

note: Only before nouns: 옛 친구, 옛 추억.

ex.en: I ran into an old friend on the street yesterday.

ex.s: 이 동네는 옛 모습이 많이 남아 있어요.
ex.en: This neighborhood still keeps a lot of its old look.

ex.s: 이 노래를 들으면 옛 추억이 생각나요.
ex.en: This song brings back old memories.

note: 배송비 shipping fee; 무료 배송 free shipping.

ex.en: When will my order be delivered?
This store has free shipping.
I checked the delivery tracking on my phone.
We took a walk at the lake park on the weekend.
We booked a place near the lake.
Have you ever gone boating on the lake?

note: 공지사항 notices; 공지하다 to announce.

ex.en: I posted a notice in the group chat.
Be sure to check the school notice.
The company sent out a notice about time off.

en: to touch, reach; get in touch

ex.s: 키가 작아서 선반에 손이 안 닿아요.
ex.en: I'm short, so I can't reach the shelf.
My bag touched the person next to me on the subway.

ex.s: 그 친구랑 연락이 닿으면 알려 주세요.
ex.en: Let me know if you get in touch with that friend.

note: 정신(을) 차리다: to pull oneself together.

ex.en: Mom made dinner for us.
I'll set the table before the guests arrive.
My friend opened a café in the neighborhood.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 더러워요.

ex.en: My shoes are really dirty.
The restaurant's restroom was a bit dirty.
Put your dirty clothes in the washing machine.

note: Adverb 영원히 'forever' is very common.

ex.en: Nothing in the world lasts forever.
Our friendship will last forever.
I wish this moment would last forever.
I'm promoting my shop on social media.
I helped promote my friend's show.
It's a poster promoting the school festival.

note: Lunar August 15; families gather and eat 송편.

ex.en: Are you going back to your hometown for Chuseok?
I'm going on a trip over the Chuseok holiday.
The shops are all closed because it's Chuseok.

note: Often with negatives or 'why': 굳이 안 해도 돼요.

ex.en: You really don't have to come.
You really don't need to buy a gift.
Why did you go and buy the expensive one?

note: Used for products; everyday words are 색 and 색깔.

ex.en: Do you have this in other colors?
The new car is a nice color.
Did you pick a color for your phone case?
I'll eat half the pizza tomorrow.
Half my salary goes to rent.
I've finished about half my homework.
In spring we go see the cherry blossoms.
I need to buy some spring clothes.
This spring was a bit cold.

note: 북쪽 north, 동쪽 east, 서쪽 west.

ex.en: Busan is south of Seoul.
Go straight south and you'll reach the sea.

ex.s: 겨울에는 따뜻한 남쪽으로 여행 가고 싶어요.
ex.en: In winter I want to travel somewhere warm down south.
Did you brush your teeth before bed?
Could you wipe the table?
Even after cleaning my glasses, I can't see well.

note: Often misused for 다르다 'different' in casual speech.

ex.en: I was wrong. Sorry.
I got two questions wrong on the test.
I think the delivery address is wrong.

note: 제한하다 to limit; 나이 제한 age limit.

ex.s: 이 식당은 두 시간 제한이 있어요.
ex.en: This restaurant has a two-hour limit.
What's the baggage weight limit?
We limit the kids' gaming time.

ex.s: 이 서류 좀 부장님께 전달해 주세요.
ex.en: Please pass this document on to the manager.

ex.s: 엄마한테 제 말 좀 전달해 줘요.
ex.en: Please pass my message on to Mom.
The courier says he left it with the security office.

en: to splash, spatter; to stand out

ex.en: Watch out, the oil splatters.
Water splashed when a car went by.
That outfit stands out a bit too much.
I looked up the word I didn't know in the dictionary.
I'll look for a pharmacy nearby.
Look up travel info in advance.
It's a little chilly today.

ex.s: 아기 자니까 문을 살짝 닫아 주세요.
ex.en: The baby's sleeping, so please close the door gently.
It's slightly spicy, but tasty.
These days I don't have time to talk with my kid.
Having conversations in Korean is still hard for me.
I talked with my team leader before the meeting.

note: 감동받다/감동하다 to be moved; 감동적이다 moving.

ex.en: I was really moved by that movie.
I was touched by my husband's birthday letter.
Yesterday's performance was really moving.
Just go 100 meters from here.
I swam 500 meters at the pool today.

ex.s: 그 산은 높이가 천 미터쯤 돼요.
ex.en: That mountain is about a thousand meters high.

note: Before vowel endings use 머무르다: 머물러요.

ex.en: I'll stay in Seoul for a week.
I decided to stay at a friend's place for a few days.
Which hotel are you staying at now?
Some of my friends are already here.
Some shops are closed on Sundays.
Only a few people came to the meeting.

note: Everyday speech often says 커플 or 애인.

ex.en: There are lots of couples in the park.
Those two went from friends to a couple.
It's a great restaurant for couples.
We took family photos at a studio.
These days I go to a yoga studio.
My friend works at a recording studio.
I definitely left it here, but it's gone.
I clearly told you.
They definitely said it would rain tomorrow.

note: 해수욕장: a beach for swimming.

ex.en: In the evening we walked along the beach.
We booked a hotel near the beach.
If the weather's nice, let's go to the beach.
It's cold, so sleep with a blanket on.
Cover the leftovers with plastic wrap.
I closed the book and rested for a bit.
That's a good idea!
Any ideas for a birthday present?
I came up with a new idea at the meeting.

en: to go badly; to be a pity
note: One word here (안됐네요); 안 되다 'not allowed' is spaced.

ex.en: That's too bad. Are you okay?
Business hasn't been going well lately.
You look really worn out.
My friend suggested we travel together.
I proposed a new approach at the meeting.
Suggest something for lunch.

en: to wear (ring, gloves, glasses); get stuck

ex.en: I wore my wedding ring today.
It was cold, so I put on gloves.
I've got red pepper flakes stuck in my teeth.
Wait a bit. I'll be right there.
White clothes get dirty fast.
I just ate, so I'm full.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 조심스러워요; adverb 조심스럽게.

ex.en: I opened the door carefully.
That topic is a bit delicate.
I held the baby carefully.
Prices are shown in English too.
An error message appeared on the screen.
Our hotel is marked on the map.

note: For a fitness gym, people usually say 헬스장.

ex.en: We played basketball in the school gym.
The graduation is held in the gymnasium.
On weekends I play badminton at the local gym.
Please put the sauce on the side.
This sauce is really good.
Do we have tomato sauce in the fridge?

note: 계좌 번호 account number; 계좌 이체 bank transfer.

ex.en: Please send me your account number.
I opened a new account at the bank.
I'll send the rent to your account.
We decorated the Christmas tree together.
I dressed up a bit because I have a date today.
We decorated the new office nicely.
My friend showed off his new car.
Mom bragged about my grades.
My coworker showed off photos of her baby.

note: More formal than 아이; honorific 자녀분.

ex.en: How many children do you have?
How old is your child?
I care a lot about my kids' education.
Don't judge people by their looks.
The doctor decided surgery was necessary.
Decide for yourself what to do.

note: Also 초록색; 녹색불 green (traffic) light.

ex.en: Cross when the light is green.
The green shirt looks good on you.
We painted the wall light green.

note: More formal than 사다; common online and in stores.

ex.en: I purchased the tickets online.

ex.s: 이 상품은 한 사람당 두 개까지 구매할 수 있어요.
ex.en: You can buy up to two of these per person.
I'm planning to buy a new laptop.

en: to follow, go along; keep up

ex.en: Follow the car in front.
It's hard to keep up with the class.
The kid wants to go along with Mom.
I barely caught the bus.
I only slept five hours last night.
I just barely finished my homework.

note: Two different words: 電源 'power', 全員 'all members'.

ex.en: My phone died.
Press the computer's power button.
Our whole family attended the wedding.

note: Pork is 돼지고기.

ex.en: We saw pigs at the farm.
Want some pork kimchi stew?

ex.s: 너무 많이 먹어서 돼지가 된 것 같아요.
ex.en: I ate so much I feel like a pig.
That store is open until midnight.
I got home after midnight.
Submit your homework by midnight.
Could you press the elevator button?
Press the red button to turn it off.

ex.s: 이 앱에서 저장 버튼이 어디 있어요?
ex.en: Where's the save button in this app?

note: 출시되다 to be released, come out.

ex.en: The new phone comes out next month.
When did this snack come out?
There's a discount to celebrate the new menu launch.

en: rather, would rather, might as well

ex.en: We'd be better off taking a taxi.
I'd rather eat at home today.
If it's going to be like this, I'd rather not go.
This is a common mistake.
People commonly catch colds in winter.

ex.s: 이 이름은 한국에서 흔히 볼 수 있어요.
ex.en: You often see this name in Korea.

note: 고개를 끄덕이다 nod; 고개를 숙이다 bow one's head.

ex.en: Minho nodded.

ex.s: 사진 찍게 고개 좀 들어 봐요.
ex.en: Lift your head a bit for the photo.
I bowed my head in greeting.
Hold on tight to the handle.
The subway was packed with people.
Please close the lid tightly.
Let's have a serious talk.
Why are you so serious?

ex.s: 케빈 씨는 일할 때 아주 진지해요.
ex.en: Kevin is very serious when he works.

note: Also 목록.

ex.en: I made a grocery list.
I have a list of places I want to travel to.
Please send me the attendee list.

note: Loanword; 색 and 색깔 are more everyday.

ex.en: I want to dye my hair this color.
Color prints are 200 won a page.
What's the trending color this year?

note: 춤 is the general word.

ex.en: I take classes at a dance studio after work.
My daughter learns dance after school.
That idol's dancing skills are amazing.

note: Also a noun: 높이 'height'.

ex.en: I threw the ball high.

ex.s: 질문 있으면 손을 높이 들어 주세요.
ex.en: If you have a question, raise your hand high.
The kite is flying high in the sky.
Willpower is key when dieting.
Ji-woo has strong willpower.
These days I can't find the will to study.
There are separate restrooms for men and women.
This clothing is unisex.
Our class has about as many boys as girls.

ex.s: 차 고치는 데 백만 원 들었어요.
ex.en: It cost a million won to fix the car.
That video got over a million views.
You bought a million-won watch?

ex.s: 필름 카메라로 사진 찍는 게 취미예요.
ex.en: Taking pictures with a film camera is my hobby.
I put a screen protector on my phone.
I went to the photo shop to develop film.
Who's your favorite artist?
I bought tickets to that artist's concert.
My friend is a makeup artist.

note: Usually 구체적으로 'specifically' or 구체적인 + noun.

ex.en: Please be a little more specific.
Have you made concrete plans for the trip?
Please explain exactly where it hurts.

note: 매력적이다; 매력적인 + noun.

ex.s: 웨이 씨는 웃는 모습이 정말 매력적이에요.
ex.en: Wei has a really charming smile.
This city is a really charming place.
It's a company with an attractive salary.

note: 대표적인 + noun; 대표적으로 'a prime example is'.

ex.en: Bibimbap is a classic Korean dish.
It's this neighborhood's best-known café.
A typical cold symptom is coughing.

note: 별도로 separately; 별도 요금 extra charge.

ex.en: Shipping is extra.
Drinks have to be ordered separately.
There's a separate charge for hotel parking.

note: ~는 경향이 있다: to tend to.

ex.en: I tend to go to bed late.

ex.s: 요즘 젊은 사람들은 혼자 여행하는 경향이 있어요.
ex.en: Young people these days tend to travel alone.

ex.s: 그 친구는 말을 과장하는 경향이 있어요.
ex.en: That friend tends to exaggerate.
They say the heat will last until next week.

ex.s: 기침이 일주일 넘게 지속되면 병원에 가세요.
ex.en: If the cough lasts over a week, see a doctor.
The meeting went on for three whole hours.
That drama airs every Friday.
A restaurant in our neighborhood was on TV.
The final will be broadcast live.

note: 보조 배터리 = portable charger (power bank).

ex.s: 보조 배터리 있어요? 휴대폰이 꺼질 것 같아요.
ex.en: Do you have a power bank? My phone's about to die.
On weekends I work as a kitchen assistant at a restaurant.
My company subsidizes our lunches.
That singer debuted in 2015.
My friend's younger sibling debuted as an actor.
It's been ten years since this group debuted.
Try looking at it from a different point of view.
From the child's point of view, it makes sense.
We see things a bit differently.

note: 등장하다 to appear, show up.

ex.en: The scene where the main character first appears is cool.
When the singer came out, the audience screamed.
My friend suddenly showed up at the get-together.
We walked along a path through the woods.
Take this trail and you'll reach the lake.
Every morning I jog on the path in the park.

note: Adverb 상당히 'quite, fairly' is very common.

ex.en: The moving costs were considerable.
That restaurant's food is quite good.
You're quite a good driver.

note: Standard way Koreans describe home and shop sizes.

ex.en: How many pyeong is this apartment?
My friend moved to a 30-pyeong apartment.

ex.s: 가게가 열 평 정도라서 좀 작아요.
ex.en: The shop is only about 10 pyeong, so it's a bit small.
